correctness.rationale: A complete finite-dimensional piecewise-affine KKT derivation computes each row coefficient and optimizes all strict faces. Explicit strict-feasible inputs realize the maximizing Jacobian row as a finite-pair gain. Exact rational face enumeration of 340 small size patterns and separate numerical projection tests supplement, not substitute for, the proof. Radius-zero and overlapping-group exceptions are excluded.

originality.rationale: Six primary papers on exactly the relevant group-supremum projection, its proximal dual, or computationally different multilevel maps were inspected. Their KKT algorithms are acknowledged, and their stated results do not give the exact sharp global coordinatewise modulus and group-size dichotomy. Closest published published-finding corpus records concern different maps or the singleton block special case; novelty beyond accessible sources remains an explicit risk.
residual_risks: An older sensitivity theorem with another group-norm name or a more general polyhedral projection theorem could imply this coefficient without repeating its formula.
Record matching and targeted literature inspection cannot certify universal historical novelty.

value.rationale: The exact coefficient supplies a non-Euclidean endpoint error budget for joint-sparsity projection, establishes the sharp two-group versus three-group transition, and reduces an otherwise high-dimensional face optimization to sorting block sizes. The increasing sensitivity under wider blocks is a substantive geometric effect and useful structural design constraint.
